title: Private deployments: VPC & on-prem reference, packaging, day-2 ops, upgrade and rollback
author: Ava Patel
body:
Summary:

This document consolidates best practices, reference architectures, packaging options, day-2 operational procedures, and upgrade/rollback playbooks for Redwood private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It is intended for platform engineers, SREs, and customer success engineers who operate or deliver private Redwood stacks.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: VPC deployments (AWS/Azure/GCP), air-gapped on-prem installs, Helm/OCI packaging, and the operational lifecycle (day-2 ops, upgrades, rollbacks).
- Audience: eng-private-deployments, eng-sre, customer success, and customer ops teams.

Key components (naming used in examples):
- redwood-control-plane: control plane services (auth, web UI, config API)
- redwood-operator: Kubernetes operator that manages runtime components
- redwood-runtime: model-serving runtime pods (quantized runtime containers)
- redwood-proxy: edge proxy for routing and TLS termination
- redwood-metrics: Prometheus exporters and metric collectors

Prerequisites (customer/host):
- Networking: private subnets for runtime, dedicated management subnet, NAT/egress or proxy for image pulls (if required).
- IAM/KMS: customer-managed KMS (recommended) with least privilege keys for secrets and model encryption.
- Storage: block storage for model artifacts (NFS/CSI on-prem, EBS/GCP PD/Azure Disk in cloud) and object store for backups.
- Hardware (on-prem): 1- N GPU nodes (e.g., A100/H100 equivalents) + CPU workers for control plane.
- Capacity planning: expected QPS, average sequence length, peak concurrency — see Customer Requirements table below.

Reference architectures:

1) VPC (cloud) reference
- High level: customer VPC with three tiers: control (private), runtime (private with GPUs), and edge (public NIC or private with customer ALB).
- Network: separate subnets by tier, NAT gateway for runtime (or VPC endpoints for container registry), security groups restricting inter-tier traffic.
- Key items:
  - Private endpoints for S3/GCS (avoid public egress for model pulls).
  - KMS integration via IAM role or key policy and explicit KMS endpoints.
  - VPC flow logs enabled for audit.

2) On-prem (air-gapped) reference
- High level: control plane can be either customer-managed or delivered as an appliance; runtime deployed into customer Kubernetes cluster with offline OCI registries for images.
- Packaging: deliver OCI tarballs and Helm chart artifacts via secure artifact server or USB (for extreme air-gapped).
- Hardware: validated GPU node types, NVLink planning if required, and dedicated storage for model caches.

Packaging and installation options:
- Kubernetes (recommended): Helm chart + redwood-operator YAML. Charts are versioned by semver and published as OCI references.
- Container images: hosted on container registry; for air-gapped installs we provide signed OCI tarballs and an import script (import-images.sh).
- Non-Kubernetes (edge/on-prem appliance): systemd units, docker-compose for small PoCs. This is supported but not recommended for production.

Installation: step-by-step (Kubernetes / VPC)
1. Prep network and IAM: create subnets, routing, security groups, and IAM roles with policies in the customer account.
2. Provision storage: create block volumes / provision CSI storage classes.
3. Create KMS keys and grant redwood-control-plane encryption role.
4. Install redwood-operator: helm repo add redwood https://packages.redwood.ai/charts && helm install redwood-operator redwood/redwood-operator --namespace redwood-system --create-namespace --version 1.4.0
5. Deploy control plane: kubectl apply -f control-plane.yaml (control plane config references KMS, DB endpoints).
6. Configure runtime pools: apply RuntimePool CRD specifying GPU type, node selectors, autoscaling policy (min/max/target gpu-util).
7. Validate: smoke tests (see Validation section).

Air-gapped / on-prem installation highlights
- Import OCI artifacts: ./import-images.sh --tar images-v1.4.0.tar.gz --registry localhost:5000
- Configure private registry credentials in imagePullSecrets.
- Ensure NTP/time sync and GPU driver versions match packaged runtime driver matrix.

Day-2 operations (checklist and runbook items)
- Observability: ensure redwood-metrics is scraping and dashboards show p95 latency, token/sec, error rates.
- Backups: weekly metadata backup to object store + nightly DB WAL snapshots.
- Model cache warmup: after scale-up, run cache-warmup job with top N prefixes.
- Scaling: adjust RuntimePool CRD or use autoscaler (recommended thresholds: target GPU utilization 65%-75%).
- Node replacement: cordon & drain, ensure KV cache checkpointing or use cache prewarm job after replacement.
- Certificate rotation: rotate TLS certs every 90 days; use ACME for public endpoints or internal PKI for private installs.
- Log retention: forward logs to customer SIEM/ELK; preserve 90 days for security/audit by default.

Upgrade and rollback procedures
Principles:
- Adopt semantic versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH).
- Perform upgrades in non-prod, then canary (5-10% traffic), then full rollout.
- Automate health checks and be able to rollback within sliding window (default 30 minutes).

Canary upgrade steps (Kubernetes):
1. Create release tag: chart v1.5.0 and images redwood/runtime:1.5.0.
2. Deploy to staging and run full validation suite (integration, perf, prompt set test).
3. Canary deploy: update ingress/traffic-split to send 5% to new release (use redwood-traffic-split CRD or service mesh weights).
4. Monitor: p99/p95 latency, error_rate, token_loss_rate, model-determinism on validation prompts for 60 minutes.
5. Gradual rollout: 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 30-60 minute observation windows.
6. Rollback criteria: 
   - error_rate > 1% absolute, or
   - p95 latency regression > 40% relative, or
   - failed health checks / degraded model outputs on eval set.
7. Rollback action: helm rollback <release> <revision> or restore previous image tag using kubectl set image deployment/redwood-runtime redwood-runtime=<previous-image>.

Database and schema migrations
- All DB migrations are executed through the control plane migration job and are backward compatible where possible. For non-backward compatible migrations, the process requires a maintenance window and documented migration steps. Always snapshot DB before applying migrations.

Validation and quality gates
- Smoke tests: control API auth, model list, a single short generation request.
- Perf tests: 1-minute sustained workload matching 10% of peak QPS for latency profiling.
- Eval prompt set: run the canonical customer prompt set and check for output regressions (use Redwood Optimize regression harness).

Incident runbook (short form)
1. If runtime unhealthy: check redwood-runtime pod events, GPU driver errors, and redwood-operator logs.
2. If control plane degraded: check DB connectivity and KMS errors.
3. Escalate to eng-sre after 15 minutes if no remediation.
4. For critical production impact, fail traffic to fallback model variant or dedicated hosted API per routing policy.

Customer requirements library (summary table)
| Requirement Area | Minimum | Recommended | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Network | Private subnets, NAT or egress proxy | VPC endpoints for registry + object store | Flow logs + NACLs |
| Security | KMS + IAM roles | HSM/KMS integration, RBAC, Audit logs | Confidential workloads require restricted endpoints |
| Storage | 500GB block | 2TB block + object store | Depends on model size & cache policy |
| Hardware | 1 GPU for PoC | >=4 GPUs for production | Specify GPU type (A100/H100) |
| Capacity | 50 concurrent requests | capacity based on tokens/sec estimates | Provide peak concurrency and seq len |
| Support | N/A | Dedicated support SLA & runbook | 24x7 for enterprise |

Ownership and escalation
- Deployment owners: eng-private-deployments (primary), eng-sre (secondary).
- Oncall escalation: use standard oncall matrix; contact eng-private-deployments@redwood.ai for first response.

Automations and CI/CD
- Charts and images published from CI: CI pipeline tags chart + image with the same semver and creates a release artifact.
- Upgrade jobs: pipeline can trigger canary rollout and waits for metric gates.
- Import scripts for air-gapped installs are signed and verified via sha256 sums.

Validation checklist (pre-go-live)
- [ ] Network connectivity validated (registry, object store, KMS)
- [ ] Autoscaling and node types validated with load test
- [ ] Backup and restore validated from snapshot
- [ ] Eval prompt set regression check passed
- [ ] Security review and penetration test completed (if required)

Appendix: common commands and snippets
- Helm install operator: helm install redwood-operator redwood/redwood-operator --version 1.4.0 --namespace redwood-system
- Import images (air-gapped): ./import-images.sh --tar images-1.5.0.tar.gz --registry localhost:5000
- Rollback (helm): helm rollback redwood-release 2 --namespace redwood

Related documents:
- See related pages list for runbooks, detailed packaging artifacts, and reference architectures.

Contact and feedback:
- Document owner: eng-private-deployments (Ava Patel)
- For questions and deployment requests open an internal ticket with label "private-deploy" or contact the reviewer list above.
